bedfordshire.meta: Commercial glazing in Bedfordshire, from Luton Airport's business parks to Bedford town centre. Windows, doors and curtain walling from nearby Milton Keynes.
bedfordshire.lead: Bedfordshire is next door to our Milton Keynes base, and two of our published projects are here: All Hallows in Bedford and The Green Man at Eversholt.
bedfordshire.buildings: The county runs from the warehouses and distribution sites around Dunstable and the M1 to the offices and schools of Bedford. Cranfield University and the businesses around London Luton Airport add research buildings and light industrial units to the mix.
bedfordshire.site: Sites close to the airport and the M1 junctions often have fixed delivery slots and gatehouse rules. Tell us how vehicles reach the building and we can plan the frame and glass deliveries around them.
bedfordshire.q: Have you worked on commercial buildings in Bedfordshire?
bedfordshire.a: Yes. All Hallows in Bedford took automatic opening vent windows, a glazed entrance screen and steel doorsets, and The Green Man at Eversholt took twelve period-style windows. Both are in our commercial projects archive.

berkshire.meta: Commercial glazing in Berkshire for Reading offices, Slough's trading estate and Windsor's historic streets. Send your drawings for windows, doors and screens.
berkshire.lead: From Thames Valley Park to Slough Trading Estate, Berkshire's commercial buildings are busy places, and our Pincents Kiln project in Reading was fitted during an industrial unit refurbishment.
berkshire.buildings: Reading's business parks and town centre offices sit alongside the industrial units of Slough Trading Estate and Greenham Business Park at Newbury. Windsor adds hotels and shopfronts in streets around the castle, where the look of a frontage carries more weight.
berkshire.site: On a managed business park, the estate team usually sets working hours, parking and delivery routes. Send us their site rules with your schedule and we will build the programme around them.
berkshire.q: Can you match a special frame colour on a Berkshire refurbishment?
berkshire.a: Yes. At Pincents Kiln in Reading, the aluminium ribbon windows and entrance door were powder coated to a special colour to match the new cladding on the building.

bristol.meta: Commercial glazing in Bristol, from Temple Quarter offices to Clifton's period buildings and Avonmouth's industrial units. Send us your opening schedule.
bristol.lead: Bristol asks a lot of a glazing scheme: tight city streets around the harbour, listed terraces in Clifton and big industrial units out at Avonmouth.
bristol.buildings: Offices around Temple Quarter and the harbourside work alongside the aerospace businesses at Filton and the docks and warehouses at Avonmouth. Clifton and Redland hold much of the city's period stock, and many of those streets are conservation areas.
bristol.site: City centre streets can leave little room for a delivery vehicle, so tell us about loading bays, permits and lift sizes early. In Clifton, send any planning conditions that apply to the frames.
bristol.q: Can you work to planning conditions on a conservation area building in Bristol?
bristol.a: Send us the planning conditions with your drawings. Frame profile, colour and glazing bar layout can all be specified to what the local authority has asked for.

buckinghamshire.meta: Commercial glazing in Buckinghamshire from our Milton Keynes base. Windows, doors and curtain walling for Aylesbury, High Wycombe and the Chilterns.
buckinghamshire.lead: Buckinghamshire is our home ground. Our base at Bradwell Abbey is a short drive from Aylesbury, and our rail depot project at Bletchley is in Milton Keynes itself.
buckinghamshire.buildings: Aylesbury and High Wycombe hold most of the county's offices, schools and retail. Stoke Mandeville Hospital, Pinewood Studios at Iver and Westcott Venture Park show how varied the commercial buildings get once you leave the town centres.
buckinghamshire.site: Much of the south of the county lies in the Chilterns National Landscape, where planners pay close attention to how a building looks. Rural sites may also need a smaller delivery vehicle, so tell us about the approach road.
buckinghamshire.q: How quickly can you visit a site in Buckinghamshire?
buckinghamshire.a: We are based at Bradwell Abbey in Milton Keynes, so Buckinghamshire is close to home. Send the site address and your dates and we will tell you when we can attend.

cambridgeshire.meta: Commercial glazing in Cambridgeshire for science parks, college buildings and Peterborough's business estates. Send your specification to our team.
cambridgeshire.lead: Cambridgeshire's commercial buildings range from laboratories on the Cambridge Science Park to medieval streets in Ely and the business estates of Peterborough.
cambridgeshire.buildings: Cambridge Science Park and the Cambridge Biomedical Campus around Addenbrooke's bring research and healthcare buildings with demanding specifications. Alconbury Weald near Huntingdon is growing fast, and Peterborough adds logistics and office space close to the A1.
cambridgeshire.site: Research and healthcare buildings often stay in use throughout the work. Tell us which rooms are sensitive to dust, noise or vibration and when they can be released, and the sequence can follow that.
cambridgeshire.q: Can you work around laboratories or clinical areas in Cambridgeshire?
cambridgeshire.a: Tell us which areas stay in use, what they are sensitive to and when each can be released. We have fitted windows in a working hospital at Bishop's Stortford and replaced every window and door in a working care home at Kettering.

cheshire.meta: Commercial glazing in Cheshire for Chester's historic centre, Warrington's business parks and Alderley Park. Send us your drawings and schedule.
cheshire.lead: Cheshire pairs some of the North West's biggest business parks with one of England's most distinctive historic city centres.
cheshire.buildings: Birchwood Park at Warrington and Alderley Park near Macclesfield hold offices and science buildings, while Crewe and Northwich add industrial units. Chester's medieval Rows and city walls give the centre a character that any replacement frontage has to respect.
cheshire.site: Work in central Chester often means pedestrian streets, restricted delivery hours and listed building controls. Send those details with your enquiry so frame choices and deliveries can be planned around them.
cheshire.q: Can you supply glazing for a listed building in Chester?
cheshire.a: Send us the listed building consent and any conditions attached to it. The frame profile, finish and glass can then be specified against what the conservation officer has approved.

city-of-london.meta: Commercial glazing in the City of London: office refurbishments, entrances and heritage buildings, planned around the Square Mile's delivery rules.
city-of-london.lead: In the Square Mile, the delivery plan matters as much as the frame. Our nearest published project is Heal's on Tottenham Court Road, where the glazing went into the courtyard elevations.
city-of-london.buildings: The City's offices range from post-war blocks and the listed Barbican to modern towers around Bank and Liverpool Street. Entrances here take heavy daily use, and protected views of St Paul's shape what can change on many buildings.
city-of-london.site: Vehicles enter the Congestion Charge zone, and lorries over 12 tonnes need an HGV Safety Permit. Tell us about loading bays, goods lift sizes, building manager rules and out-of-hours access before the programme is set.
city-of-london.q: Can you deliver to a building in the City with no loading bay?
city-of-london.a: Tell us what access the building has, including goods lifts, street restrictions and permitted hours. Deliveries can then be split and timed to suit, with sizes checked against the route through the building.

cornwall.meta: Commercial glazing in Cornwall for hotels, healthcare and coastal premises. Frames and finishes specified for how close the building is to the sea.
cornwall.lead: In Cornwall, the first question for any frame is how close the building stands to the sea, because that decides the finish worth specifying.
cornwall.buildings: Hotels and restaurants around Newquay, Falmouth and St Ives sit alongside the Royal Cornwall Hospital at Treliske and town centre retail in Truro. Parts of the county also fall within the Cornish Mining World Heritage Site, which brings its own planning considerations.
cornwall.site: Give us the building's distance from the shore and how exposed each elevation is. Those two details guide the powder coat, hardware and glazing specification, and seasonal trade will shape when a hotel can release its rooms.
cornwall.q: What frame finish suits a coastal building in Cornwall?
cornwall.a: It depends on how far the building is from the sea and which way it faces. Tell us both and we can specify the powder coat and hardware for that exposure before the job is priced.

cumbria.meta: Commercial glazing in Cumbria for Carlisle, Barrow, Kendal and Lake District premises. Windows and doors specified for exposed sites.
cumbria.lead: Cumbria's commercial buildings face some of England's most exposed weather, from the west coast at Whitehaven to hotels high in the Lake District.
cumbria.buildings: Carlisle holds the county's main offices and public buildings, while Barrow-in-Furness and the coast around Whitehaven are shaped by shipbuilding and the nuclear industry at Sellafield. Hotels and visitor businesses dominate the Lake District, a World Heritage Site.
cumbria.site: Tell us the elevation's exposure and the height of the building so wind loading can be considered in the specification. Narrow lanes in the Lakes may also limit the size of vehicle that can reach the site.
cumbria.q: Can you work on a hotel in the Lake District?
cumbria.a: Send us the address, the planning position and the dates the hotel can release its rooms. National park planning rules and access on narrow roads both need settling before the frames are ordered.

derbyshire.meta: Commercial glazing in Derbyshire for Derby's engineering sites, schools and Peak District premises. Send your opening schedule and drawings.
derbyshire.lead: Derbyshire takes in the engineering sites of Derby, the mills of a World Heritage valley and visitor businesses across the Peak District.
derbyshire.buildings: Derby's commercial life is tied to engineering, with Rolls-Royce the best known name, and the city has schools, offices and healthcare buildings to match. Buxton's Georgian Crescent and the Derwent Valley Mills show how much of the county's stock is protected.
derbyshire.site: Within the Peak District National Park and the Derwent Valley, planning authorities look closely at frame style and colour. Send any conditions with your enquiry so the specification starts from what has been approved.
derbyshire.q: Can you replace windows in a former mill building in Derbyshire?
derbyshire.a: Send us drawings, photographs and any planning or listed building conditions. Large openings in mill buildings are usually specified window by window, so an opening schedule is the best place to start.

devon.meta: Commercial glazing in Devon for Exeter, Plymouth and coastal hotels. Windows, doors and screens specified for the building's exposure.
devon.lead: Devon has two coasts, two cities and a wide spread of hotels, healthcare buildings and business parks between them.
devon.buildings: Exeter Science Park and the city's offices contrast with Plymouth, where Devonport Naval Base and Derriford Hospital are major sites. Torquay and the resorts along both coasts bring hotels and leisure buildings that trade to a seasonal pattern.
devon.site: On the coast, tell us how exposed the building is so frame finishes and hardware suit the position. Hotels and holiday businesses usually prefer work outside the main season, so share your preferred window early.
devon.q: Can glazing work on a Devon hotel be done out of season?
devon.a: Tell us the dates the building can release rooms or close areas. Frames are made to order, so giving us those dates early lets the order be timed to your quiet period.

dorset.meta: Commercial glazing in Dorset for Bournemouth hotels, Poole's harbourside and shops along the Jurassic Coast. Send us your site details.
dorset.lead: Dorset's commercial buildings are largely shaped by the coast, from Bournemouth's seafront hotels to the harbourside at Poole.
dorset.buildings: Bournemouth and Poole hold most of the county's offices, retail and hotels, with Bournemouth University adding education buildings. Further west, Dorchester and Weymouth serve towns along the Jurassic Coast, a natural World Heritage Site.
dorset.site: Share how close the building stands to the sea and which elevations take the weather. In resort towns, seafront parking and summer footfall can both affect how materials reach the site.
dorset.q: Can you replace entrance doors while a Dorset shop stays open?
dorset.a: Tell us the trading hours, how customers use the entrance and whether a second door is available. The replacement can then be planned around the times the shop is quietest.

durham.meta: Commercial glazing in County Durham for Durham city, Darlington and NETPark. Windows, doors and curtain walling for schools and business sites.
durham.lead: County Durham runs from Durham's World Heritage cathedral to the science buildings at NETPark and the rail engineering of Newton Aycliffe.
durham.buildings: Durham University and the historic peninsula dominate the city, while Darlington and Bishop Auckland have offices, schools and public buildings. NETPark at Sedgefield and Hitachi Rail's plant at Newton Aycliffe add modern industrial and research sites.
durham.site: Around Durham Cathedral and Castle, planning controls are strict and streets are narrow and steep. Elsewhere in the county, schools usually want the noisiest work kept to holidays, so include term dates with your enquiry.
durham.q: Can you fit windows in a school during the holidays?
durham.a: Yes. At Midfield Primary School in Orpington, eight windows and a double door were fitted over the October half term. Send us your term dates and the rooms involved.

east-riding-of-yorkshire.meta: Commercial glazing across Hull and the East Riding for port buildings, schools and retail. Frames specified for the Humber's exposed sites.
east-riding-of-yorkshire.lead: Hull and the East Riding combine a working port on the Humber with market towns such as Beverley and a long, exposed North Sea coast.
east-riding-of-yorkshire.buildings: Hull's docks and the offshore wind blade factory at Alexandra Dock anchor the area's industry, with the University of Hull and the city's offices nearby. Beverley's Minster and market streets contrast with seaside premises at Bridlington.
east-riding-of-yorkshire.site: Port sites normally have their own security checks and vehicle rules, so tell us about passes and inductions in advance. On the coast and the estuary, let us know how exposed each elevation is.
east-riding-of-yorkshire.q: Can you work on a site inside a port or secure estate?
east-riding-of-yorkshire.a: Send us the site's induction, pass and vehicle requirements with your enquiry so they can be built into the programme before any work is booked.

east-sussex.meta: Commercial glazing in East Sussex for Brighton's seafront, Eastbourne's hotels and Lewes's historic streets. Send your drawings to our team.
east-sussex.lead: East Sussex is defined by its seafront: Regency terraces in Brighton, grand hotels in Eastbourne and a coastline that tests every frame and fitting.
east-sussex.buildings: Brighton mixes offices, hospitality and the University of Sussex at Falmer with the Royal Pavilion and streets of protected Regency buildings. Eastbourne, Hastings and Bexhill bring seaside hotels and shops, and Lewes has a tightly packed historic centre.
east-sussex.site: Many seafront buildings in Brighton and Hove are listed or in conservation areas, so send any conditions with your drawings. Tell us how exposed each elevation is, and whether deliveries need a parking suspension.
east-sussex.q: Can you match existing windows on a Regency building in Brighton?
east-sussex.a: Send photographs, drawings and any planning conditions. Heritage aluminium systems and glazing bars can be specified to follow the original layout, subject to what the council has approved.

essex.meta: Commercial glazing in Essex for Chelmsford offices, Harlow's science park and retail sites. Our Herts and Essex Community Hospital project is nearby.
essex.lead: Essex covers commuter towns, big retail parks and major transport hubs, and our Herts and Essex Community Hospital project sits right on its border at Bishop's Stortford.
essex.buildings: Chelmsford and Colchester hold the county's main offices and public buildings, with Harlow Innovation Park and Stansted Airport nearby. Basildon's business estates and Southend's seafront add a wide spread of industrial and hospitality premises.
essex.site: Retail parks and business estates often limit working hours, and airport sites bring security checks. Send the landlord's or estate team's rules with your schedule so the programme can follow them.
essex.q: Can you fit windows in a healthcare building that stays open?
essex.a: Yes. Our work at Herts and Essex Community Hospital covered colour-matched aluminium windows and doors for the Kitwood Unit, fitted in a working hospital without interrupting it.

gloucestershire.meta: Commercial glazing in Gloucestershire for Cheltenham's Regency buildings, Gloucester Docks and Cotswold premises. Send us your drawings.
gloucestershire.lead: Gloucestershire asks for care with appearance, from Cheltenham's Regency terraces to honey-coloured Cotswold towns and the Victorian warehouses of Gloucester Docks.
gloucestershire.buildings: Gloucester and Cheltenham hold the county's offices, schools and retail, and Cheltenham's racecourse and hotels bring busy event periods. Cirencester, Stroud and Tewkesbury have historic centres, and much of the east lies in the Cotswolds National Landscape.
gloucestershire.site: In Cotswold stone towns, planners often look closely at frame colour and profile. In Cheltenham, event weeks can affect access and hotel availability, so tell us about any dates to avoid.
gloucestershire.q: Which frames suit a stone building in the Cotswolds?
gloucestershire.a: That depends on the building and what the planning authority will approve. Send photographs and any conditions, and we can suggest slim aluminium or heritage profiles that suit the openings.

greater-london.meta: Commercial glazing across Greater London: schools, offices and shopfronts, with deliveries planned around ULEZ and lorry controls.
greater-london.lead: Our published work in London includes classroom windows at Midfield Primary School in Orpington and courtyard glazing at Heal's on Tottenham Court Road.
greater-london.buildings: Outer London town centres such as Croydon, Ealing and Romford mix offices, shopfronts and schools with busy high streets. Further in, older buildings and tighter streets make access the first thing to settle on almost every project.
greater-london.site: The Ultra Low Emission Zone covers every borough, and the London Lorry Control Scheme controls the routes lorries over 18 tonnes can take at night and at weekends. Tell us about loading, red routes and parking suspensions before dates are agreed.
greater-london.q: Can you carry out school glazing work in London during half term?
greater-london.a: Yes. At Midfield Primary School in Orpington, eight uPVC casement windows and an aluminium double door were fitted over the October half term so the classrooms were ready when pupils returned.

greater-manchester.meta: Commercial glazing across Greater Manchester's boroughs: Bolton, Stockport, Oldham, Wigan and Trafford Park. Send your schedule to our team.
greater-manchester.lead: Beyond the city centre, Greater Manchester is a patchwork of town centres, former mills and some of the North West's largest industrial estates.
greater-manchester.buildings: Trafford Park is one of Europe's oldest planned industrial estates, and MediaCityUK in Salford brings modern offices and studios. Bolton, Oldham, Rochdale and Stockport hold schools, healthcare buildings and converted mills across their town centres.
greater-manchester.site: Former mills often have large, repeating openings, so an opening schedule with sizes and photographs is the quickest way to start. On industrial estates, tell us about shift patterns and vehicle movements around the building.
greater-manchester.q: Can you supply windows for a mill conversion in Greater Manchester?
greater-manchester.a: Send drawings, an opening schedule and any planning conditions. We supplied aluminium windows for the conversion of four office buildings into student studios at Headrow Court in Leeds, and repeat openings are planned in a similar way.

hampshire.meta: Commercial glazing in Hampshire for Southampton, Portsmouth, Winchester and Basingstoke. Windows, doors and screens for offices and public buildings.
hampshire.lead: Hampshire stretches from the working ports of the Solent to Winchester's cathedral close and the business parks around Basingstoke and Farnborough.
hampshire.buildings: Southampton's docks and Portsmouth's naval base and Historic Dockyard shape the south of the county, alongside their universities. Basingstoke and Farnborough hold offices and aerospace businesses, while Winchester's centre is full of protected buildings.
hampshire.site: Near the Solent, tell us how exposed the building is so frame finishes can be chosen accordingly. Defence, port and airport sites will have their own security checks, which need building into the programme.
hampshire.q: Can you work on secure sites in Hampshire?
hampshire.a: Send the site's security, induction and vehicle requirements with your enquiry. They can then be planned into the programme before dates are agreed.

herefordshire.meta: Commercial glazing in Herefordshire for Hereford's Skylon Park, schools, rural businesses and market towns. Send your site details to our team.
herefordshire.lead: Herefordshire is rural, with black-and-white market towns, working farms and the growing Enterprise Zone at Skylon Park on the edge of Hereford.
herefordshire.buildings: Hereford holds the cathedral, the county hospital and most of the offices and shops. Leominster, Ledbury and Ross-on-Wye have historic high streets, and rural schools and converted farm buildings make up much of the county's smaller commercial work.
herefordshire.site: Country lanes can limit the size of delivery vehicle, so tell us about the approach and any weight or height restrictions. Parts of the south fall within the Wye Valley National Landscape, where appearance gets close attention.
herefordshire.q: Can you deliver large frames to a rural site in Herefordshire?
herefordshire.a: Tell us about the approach road, turning space and any height or weight limits. Frame sizes and the delivery vehicle can then be planned around what the site can take.

hertfordshire.meta: Commercial glazing in Hertfordshire, where we have completed St Albans School and the Herts and Essex Community Hospital. Send your schedule.
hertfordshire.lead: Hertfordshire is close to our base, and we have completed curtain walling at St Albans School and aluminium windows at the Herts and Essex Community Hospital here.
hertfordshire.buildings: Watford, Stevenage and Hatfield Business Park hold the county's offices and science-based employers, including GSK's research site on Gunnels Wood Road in Stevenage. St Albans and Hitchin have historic centres, and schools are a large part of the commercial work.
hertfordshire.site: Schools and hospitals usually need work phased around people using the building. Send term dates or clinical constraints with your drawings, and tell us which rooms can be released and when.
hertfordshire.q: What have you done at schools in Hertfordshire?
hertfordshire.a: At St Albans School we fitted a Smart MC600 Plus curtain wall to replace an outdated timber system in the school hall, with a fire exit door, finger guards and blackout film.

kent.meta: Commercial glazing in Kent for Maidstone offices, Canterbury's historic centre and sites near the Channel ports. Send your drawings to our team.
kent.lead: Kent runs from business parks near the M25 to the Channel ports, with Canterbury and its World Heritage cathedral in between.
kent.buildings: Kings Hill near Maidstone and Discovery Park at Sandwich hold offices and science buildings, while Bluewater and the retail parks around Dartford bring large public entrances. Canterbury and Tunbridge Wells have historic centres, and Dover's port shapes the east of the county.
kent.site: Traffic around the Channel ports can affect delivery times, so allow for it in the programme. In Canterbury, conservation controls apply to many buildings around the cathedral, so send any conditions with your enquiry.
kent.q: Can you work on a school in Kent during term time?
kent.a: Tell us which rooms can be released and when. Our Midfield Primary School project in nearby Orpington was fitted over the October half term so classrooms were ready for pupils coming back.

lancashire.meta: Commercial glazing in Lancashire for Preston, Blackpool, Lancaster and the county's industrial sites. Windows, doors and screens to your schedule.
lancashire.lead: Lancashire combines aerospace and manufacturing inland with Blackpool's seafront and a university city at Lancaster.
lancashire.buildings: BAE Systems' sites at Warton and Samlesbury lead the county's industry, and Preston holds offices, public buildings and a large university campus. Former mill towns such as Burnley and Blackburn have schools, workshops and converted industrial buildings.
lancashire.site: Blackpool's seafront is busiest in the season and during the Illuminations, so tell us about any dates to avoid. On the coast, let us know how exposed each elevation is.
lancashire.q: Can you work on a seafront building in Blackpool?
lancashire.a: Send the address, the dates the building can release rooms and details of the seafront exposure. The frame finish and the programme can then be planned around them.

leeds.meta: Commercial glazing in Leeds, where we fitted aluminium windows for 108 student studios at Headrow Court, opposite Leeds Town Hall.
leeds.lead: We know Leeds city centre first hand: at Headrow Court, opposite the Town Hall, we supplied aluminium windows for four former office buildings converted into 108 student studios.
leeds.buildings: The city core mixes Victorian arcades and civic buildings with newer offices at Wellington Place and apartments around Leeds Dock. The universities and teaching hospitals, including St James's and the General Infirmary, make education and healthcare a large share of the work.
leeds.site: City centre projects depend on loading space, crane or hoist access and traffic management. Tell us what has been agreed with the council and the building's neighbours before delivery dates are fixed.
leeds.q: What did you do at Headrow Court in Leeds?
leeds.a: We supplied aluminium windows for the conversion of four former office buildings into 108 student studios opposite Leeds Town Hall. The full project is in our commercial projects archive.

leicestershire.meta: Commercial glazing in Leicestershire for Leicester, Loughborough and logistics parks such as Magna Park. Send your opening schedule to our team.
leicestershire.lead: Leicestershire sits at the heart of the country's logistics network, with Magna Park at Lutterworth and East Midlands Gateway among the biggest sites in the region.
leicestershire.buildings: Warehouses and distribution sites line the M1 and M69, each with offices and entrance screens of their own. Leicester and Loughborough add large university estates, along with schools, hospitals and city centre retail.
leicestershire.site: Logistics sites run around the clock, so vehicle routes and yard safety rules come first. Send the site rules and shift patterns, and tell us which entrances must stay open throughout.
leicestershire.q: Can you replace office glazing at a working distribution site?
leicestershire.a: Tell us the shift patterns, yard rules and which entrances must stay in use. The work can then be sequenced so vehicle movements carry on around it.

lincolnshire.meta: Commercial glazing in Lincolnshire for Lincoln's historic city, Grimsby's port and coastal premises. Send us your drawings and site details.
lincolnshire.lead: Lincolnshire is one of England's largest counties, so every project starts with the same question: where is the site, and how do we reach it?
lincolnshire.buildings: Lincoln's cathedral quarter and university sit at the centre, with RAF stations at Waddington and Coningsby among the county's major sites. Grimsby and Scunthorpe bring port and industrial buildings, and Skegness has hotels and holiday premises on the coast.
lincolnshire.site: Long distances make delivery planning important, so give us the full site address and access details at the start. On the east coast, tell us how exposed each elevation is.
lincolnshire.q: Do you cover the whole of Lincolnshire?
lincolnshire.a: Send the site address and the scope of work. We review projects across the county and will tell you early whether the job is one we can take on.

manchester.meta: Commercial glazing in Manchester city centre: Ancoats, Spinningfields and the Oxford Road corridor. Send drawings and your access plan to our team.
manchester.lead: Manchester city centre packs converted mills, glass offices and two universities into a tight grid, so access planning shapes every glazing project here.
manchester.buildings: Spinningfields and the area around Deansgate hold modern offices, and Ancoats and the Northern Quarter are full of converted mills and warehouses. The Oxford Road corridor links the universities with Manchester Royal Infirmary, making education and healthcare major clients.
manchester.site: Streets in Ancoats and the Northern Quarter leave little room for vehicles, and many buildings are in conservation areas. Tell us about loading, hoists, road closures and any planning conditions before the programme is set.
manchester.q: Can you replace windows in a converted mill in Ancoats?
manchester.a: Send us drawings, an opening schedule and any planning conditions. Mill openings tend to repeat across a building, which makes a clear schedule the quickest way to reach a price.

merseyside.meta: Commercial glazing in Merseyside for Liverpool's waterfront, the Knowledge Quarter and Wirral's businesses. Send your schedule to our team.
merseyside.lead: Merseyside's buildings tell the story of a great port, from the Royal Albert Dock to the modern research buildings of Liverpool's Knowledge Quarter.
merseyside.buildings: Liverpool's business district and waterfront combine Victorian offices with new development, and the Knowledge Quarter brings universities and the Royal Liverpool University Hospital together. Birkenhead, Bootle and St Helens add industrial, public and retail buildings.
merseyside.site: On the waterfront, wind and salt exposure both affect the frame specification. Listed buildings are common in the city centre, so send any consent conditions with your drawings.
merseyside.q: Can you work on a listed commercial building in Liverpool?
merseyside.a: Send the listed building consent and any conditions. The frame profile, colour and glass can then be specified against what has been approved.

norfolk.meta: Commercial glazing in Norfolk for Norwich, Norwich Research Park and coastal hotels. Windows, doors and replacement glass to your schedule.
norfolk.lead: Norfolk is a county of big skies and long journeys, with Norwich and its research park at the centre and hotels strung along the coast.
norfolk.buildings: Norwich holds the cathedral, a medieval street pattern and most of the county's offices, with Norwich Research Park close by. Great Yarmouth supports the offshore energy sector, Cromer has seaside hotels and shops, and King's Lynn has a historic quayside.
norfolk.site: Coastal elevations need finishes chosen for the exposure, so tell us how close the sea is. The Broads and rural lanes can restrict larger vehicles, so describe the approach to the site.
norfolk.q: Can you replace glass in an existing commercial building in Norfolk?
norfolk.a: Yes. Send photographs, the marks on the glass, approximate sizes and details of access, and we can look at replacement sealed units or larger panes in the existing frames.

north-yorkshire.meta: Commercial glazing in North Yorkshire for York's historic centre, Harrogate's hotels and Scarborough's seafront. Send your drawings to our team.
north-yorkshire.lead: North Yorkshire's commercial work is often about old buildings: York's medieval streets, Harrogate's Victorian hotels and Scarborough's grand seafront.
north-yorkshire.buildings: York holds the Minster, city walls and a large regeneration site at York Central, with two universities nearby. Harrogate's Convention Centre and hotels serve a busy events calendar, and market towns such as Ripon and Northallerton have schools and shops.
north-yorkshire.site: Central York has pedestrian zones and strict conservation controls, so deliveries need planning around permitted hours. In Harrogate, tell us about event dates that affect hotel availability and access.
north-yorkshire.q: Can you supply windows for a hotel in Harrogate?
north-yorkshire.a: Send the opening schedule and the dates rooms can be released. We fitted 37 aluminium windows and new entrance doors at The Barn Hotel in Coventry, and a project in a trading hotel can be planned around your bookings.

northamptonshire.meta: Commercial glazing in Northamptonshire, where we replaced every window and door at Sunrise Care Home in Kettering. Based nearby in Milton Keynes.
northamptonshire.lead: Northamptonshire is on our doorstep. At Sunrise Care Home in Kettering we replaced every window and door while residents stayed in the building.
northamptonshire.buildings: Logistics sites around DIRFT at Daventry and along the M1 sit alongside Northampton's offices and schools. Silverstone brings motorsport and engineering businesses to the south of the county, with Kettering, Corby and Wellingborough adding industrial estates and healthcare buildings.
northamptonshire.site: Occupied buildings need a clear plan for each room. Tell us who stays in the building, which areas can be released and when, and we can phase the work around them.
northamptonshire.q: Can you work in a care home while residents stay in?
northamptonshire.a: Yes. At Sunrise Care Home in Kettering, a working dementia care home, every window and door was replaced in phases around the residents, who stayed in the building throughout.

northumberland.meta: Commercial glazing in Northumberland for Morpeth, Blyth, Hexham and Alnwick. Windows and doors specified for exposed northern sites.
northumberland.lead: Northumberland is England's least densely populated county, with long distances, an exposed coast and some of the country's most protected landscapes.
northumberland.buildings: Cramlington's business parks and specialist emergency care hospital sit near the county's southern edge, close to the Port of Blyth. Alnwick and Hexham have historic market centres, and Hadrian's Wall, a World Heritage Site, crosses the south of the county.
northumberland.site: Allow for distance and weather when planning deliveries, and give us the exact site location. On the coast and upland sites, tell us how exposed each elevation is so the specification suits it.
northumberland.q: Do you take on projects as far north as Northumberland?
northumberland.a: Send the site address, drawings and scope. We review each project on its details and will tell you early whether it is one we can take on.

nottinghamshire.meta: Commercial glazing in Nottinghamshire for Nottingham's Lace Market, Queen's Medical Centre and business estates. Send your schedule to our team.
nottinghamshire.lead: Nottingham's Lace Market, its two universities and one of England's largest hospitals give this county a broad mix of commercial buildings.
nottinghamshire.buildings: The Lace Market's Victorian warehouses now hold offices, apartments and college buildings, while the Queen's Medical Centre and the Boots campus at Beeston are major sites. Mansfield, Newark and Worksop add town centre premises and industrial estates.
nottinghamshire.site: The Lace Market is a conservation area, with narrow streets and tight loading. Tell us about planning conditions, vehicle access and which floors stay occupied before the work is programmed.
nottinghamshire.q: Can you work on a Lace Market building in Nottingham?
nottinghamshire.a: Send drawings, photographs and any planning conditions for the building, along with the loading arrangements. The frames and the delivery plan can then be worked out together.

oxfordshire.meta: Commercial glazing in Oxfordshire for Harwell Campus, Milton Park, Oxford's colleges and Banbury's business estates. Send us your drawings.
oxfordshire.lead: Oxfordshire pairs major science parks with some of England's most carefully protected buildings, and it is an easy journey from our Milton Keynes base.
oxfordshire.buildings: Harwell Campus and Milton Park near Didcot bring laboratories and technology businesses, while Oxford's colleges and hospitals form large, long-standing estates. Bicester and Banbury add logistics and manufacturing, and Blenheim Palace at Woodstock is a World Heritage Site.
oxfordshire.site: Central Oxford has restricted vehicle access and a Zero Emission Zone on some streets, so tell us how materials can reach the building. College work usually follows the academic calendar.
oxfordshire.q: Can you carry out work around the Oxford academic year?
oxfordshire.a: Send us the term dates and the rooms involved. Frames are made to order, so sharing the dates early lets the work be timed for the vacation.

rutland.meta: Commercial glazing in Rutland for Oakham, Uppingham, schools and rural premises. Windows and doors planned from our Milton Keynes base.
rutland.lead: Rutland is England's smallest historic county, and its commercial buildings are mostly schools, stone-built market town premises and rural businesses.
rutland.buildings: Oakham School and Uppingham School are the county's best known institutions, each with buildings from several centuries. Kendrew Barracks at Cottesmore and the hospitality businesses around Rutland Water account for much of the remaining commercial property.
rutland.site: Local limestone buildings in Oakham and Uppingham often sit in conservation areas, so send any planning conditions. Schools will want noisy work in the holidays, so include your term dates.
rutland.q: Can you match windows on a stone school building in Rutland?
rutland.a: Send photographs, drawings and any conditions. At Merchant Taylors' School we fitted heritage aluminium windows matched to the look of the originals, and the same approach can be considered here.

sheffield.meta: Commercial glazing in Sheffield for Kelham Island, the universities and city centre regeneration. Send your drawings and opening schedule.
sheffield.lead: Sheffield's commercial buildings reflect its steel history, from converted workshops at Kelham Island to the city's large university and hospital estates.
sheffield.buildings: The Heart of the City scheme has brought new offices and shops to the centre, and Kelham Island and the Cultural Industries Quarter have turned old works into homes and studios. The two universities and the Northern General Hospital are among the biggest estates.
sheffield.site: Sheffield's hills affect how a vehicle or crane can reach a site, so include photographs of the approach. In Kelham Island, older workshops may have conservation conditions to follow.
sheffield.q: Can you replace windows in a former workshop in Kelham Island?
sheffield.a: Send drawings or photographs, an opening schedule and any planning conditions. Openings in older works vary in size, so a schedule by elevation is the best place to begin.

shropshire.meta: Commercial glazing in Shropshire for Shrewsbury, Telford's business parks and heritage premises in Ironbridge and Ludlow. Send your details.
shropshire.lead: Shropshire holds the birthplace of industry at Ironbridge, a medieval county town at Shrewsbury and modern business parks at Telford.
shropshire.buildings: Telford's T54 and Hortonwood estates are among the county's main employment sites, with Harper Adams University near Newport. Shrewsbury and Ludlow have timber-framed streets, and the Ironbridge Gorge is a World Heritage Site with strict controls on change.
shropshire.site: In Shrewsbury, Ludlow and Ironbridge, tell us about planning conditions and how vehicles reach the building, because many streets are narrow. Rural sites may also need smaller deliveries.
shropshire.q: Can you work on heritage buildings in Shropshire?
shropshire.a: Send the planning or listed building conditions with your drawings, and the frame profile and finish can be specified to what has been approved.

somerset.meta: Commercial glazing in Somerset for Taunton, Bath's World Heritage streets, Yeovil and Bridgwater. Send your drawings and schedule to our team.
somerset.lead: Somerset ranges from Bath's World Heritage streets to Hinkley Point C on the coast, one of the largest construction projects in Europe.
somerset.buildings: Taunton holds the county's offices, Musgrove Park Hospital and public buildings, and Yeovil has a major helicopter manufacturing site. Bath's Georgian terraces are tightly protected, and Weston-super-Mare adds seafront hotels and shops.
somerset.site: In Bath, planning and listed building controls shape almost every external change, so send approvals with your drawings. For seaside sites, tell us how exposed each elevation is.
somerset.q: Can you supply windows for a Georgian building in Bath?
somerset.a: Send the listed building consent and drawings of the existing windows. The specification can only follow what the conservation officer has approved, so that is where the conversation starts.

south-yorkshire.meta: Commercial glazing across South Yorkshire: Doncaster, Rotherham, Barnsley and the Advanced Manufacturing Park. Send your schedule to our team.
south-yorkshire.lead: South Yorkshire's industry has moved on from coal and steel to advanced manufacturing and logistics, and its commercial buildings have changed with it.
south-yorkshire.buildings: The Advanced Manufacturing Park at Waverley brings research and engineering buildings to Rotherham, and iPort at Doncaster is a major rail-linked logistics site. Barnsley's town centre has been rebuilt around The Glass Works, and schools and hospitals serve each town.
south-yorkshire.site: Manufacturing and logistics sites run to strict safety rules, so send inductions, permit requirements and shift patterns with your enquiry. Tell us which entrances must stay open during the work.
south-yorkshire.q: Can you work at an operating manufacturing site?
south-yorkshire.a: Send the site rules, permit requirements and shift patterns. We fitted windows, doors and a curtain wall screen at a working rail depot in Bletchley, so working around live operations is familiar ground.

staffordshire.meta: Commercial glazing in Staffordshire for Stoke-on-Trent, Stafford, Lichfield and the county's manufacturers. Send your opening schedule to our team.
staffordshire.lead: Staffordshire is a manufacturing county, from the Potteries of Stoke-on-Trent to JCB's world headquarters at Rocester.
staffordshire.buildings: Stoke-on-Trent's former pottery works and bottle kilns sit among offices, schools and healthcare buildings. Keele University, Lichfield's cathedral quarter and the industrial estates around Burton, Tamworth and Cannock add to a wide commercial mix.
staffordshire.site: Older pottery buildings are often protected, so send any planning conditions with your drawings. On industrial estates, share shift patterns and vehicle routes so the work can be planned around production.
staffordshire.q: Can you replace windows at a working factory in Staffordshire?
staffordshire.a: Tell us the shift patterns, safety rules and which areas can be released. Work can then be phased so production keeps running around it.

suffolk.meta: Commercial glazing in Suffolk for Ipswich, Felixstowe's port, Adastral Park and Bury St Edmunds. Windows and doors specified for the coast.
suffolk.lead: Suffolk is home to Britain's busiest container port at Felixstowe, as well as quiet market towns and an exposed North Sea coast.
suffolk.buildings: Ipswich's waterfront and town centre hold offices, the university and public buildings, and BT's Adastral Park at Martlesham brings technology businesses. Newmarket's racing industry and Bury St Edmunds' historic centre add a very different set of premises.
suffolk.site: Port and energy sites around Felixstowe and Sizewell have strict access controls, so send their requirements with your enquiry. On the coast, tell us how exposed each elevation is.
suffolk.q: Can you work near the Port of Felixstowe?
suffolk.a: Send the site address, security requirements and access details. Vehicle bookings and passes can then be included in the programme before dates are agreed.

surrey.meta: Commercial glazing in Surrey for Guildford, Woking and Epsom: offices, schools and research buildings. Send your drawings to our team.
surrey.lead: Surrey's commercial buildings are often high specification, from Surrey Research Park in Guildford to independent schools and headquarters offices.
surrey.buildings: Guildford holds the University of Surrey, the Royal Surrey hospital and the research park, and Woking and Reigate have large office buildings serving London commuters. Independent schools and Epsom's racecourse add to a varied list of premises.
surrey.site: Much of the county lies in the Green Belt, and the Surrey Hills National Landscape brings extra attention to appearance. Near the M25, allow for traffic when planning deliveries to site.
surrey.q: Can you specify glazing for an independent school in Surrey?
surrey.a: Send drawings, term dates and any planning conditions. Our school work includes curtain walling at St Albans School and heritage aluminium windows at Merchant Taylors' School.

tyne-and-wear.meta: Commercial glazing in Tyne and Wear for Newcastle's Grainger Town, Newcastle Helix and Sunderland. Send your drawings and schedule to our team.
tyne-and-wear.lead: Tyne and Wear blends Grainger Town's classical streets with new science buildings at Newcastle Helix and major manufacturing around Sunderland.
tyne-and-wear.buildings: Newcastle's centre holds offices, two universities and the Royal Victoria Infirmary, and Newcastle Helix is a large city centre science quarter. Nissan's plant near Washington and the Port of Tyne bring major industrial sites to the wider area.
tyne-and-wear.site: Grainger Town has many listed buildings, so send any consent conditions with your drawings. Near the river and the coast at Tynemouth, tell us how exposed each elevation is.
tyne-and-wear.q: Can you work on a listed building in Grainger Town?
tyne-and-wear.a: Send the listed building consent, drawings and photographs. The specification can then follow the conditions set by the conservation officer.

warwickshire.meta: Commercial glazing in Warwickshire for Warwick, Leamington Spa, Rugby and Stratford-upon-Avon. Our Barn Hotel project in Coventry is close by.
warwickshire.lead: Warwickshire is close to our Barn Hotel project in Coventry, and it mixes motor industry sites with some of the Midlands' best known historic towns.
warwickshire.buildings: Jaguar Land Rover's site at Gaydon and Ansty Park on the edge of Coventry bring engineering and business buildings to the county. Stratford-upon-Avon's theatres and hotels, Warwick's castle town and Leamington's Regency terraces need a more careful approach.
warwickshire.site: In Stratford, Warwick and Leamington, conservation areas and listed buildings are common, so send any conditions. Hotels and visitor businesses usually have quieter periods, so tell us which dates suit you.
warwickshire.q: Can you fit windows in a hotel in Warwickshire?
warwickshire.a: Yes. At The Barn Hotel in nearby Coventry we fitted 37 aluminium windows and new entrance doors, craned in while the building was still a shell.

west-midlands.meta: Commercial glazing across the West Midlands: Birmingham, Coventry, Wolverhampton and Solihull. See our Barn Hotel project in Coventry.
west-midlands.lead: Across the West Midlands conurbation, our Barn Hotel project in Coventry is a good example of how much of the job comes down to getting glass into the building.
west-midlands.buildings: Birmingham Business Park and the National Exhibition Centre sit on the eastern side, with offices and retail across Solihull. Wolverhampton, Dudley and Walsall have town centre premises and industrial estates, and the University of Warwick is on Coventry's edge.
west-midlands.site: When a building has no internal stairs, as The Barn Hotel did, lifting needs planning from the start. Send drawings of the access and tell us whether a crane or hoist is available.
west-midlands.q: Can you crane windows into a building?
west-midlands.a: Yes. At The Barn Hotel in Coventry, 37 aluminium windows and new entrance doors were craned into a hotel that was still a shell with no stairs in it.

birmingham.meta: Commercial glazing in Birmingham for the Jewellery Quarter, Digbeth, Paradise and the city's hospitals. Send your drawings and schedule to our team.
birmingham.lead: Birmingham's centre is being rebuilt around Paradise and Digbeth, while the Jewellery Quarter's protected workshops carry on a few minutes' walk away.
birmingham.buildings: The business district around Colmore Row holds Victorian offices beside new towers, and the Jewellery Quarter is one of the city's most carefully protected conservation areas. The universities and the Queen Elizabeth Hospital form two of the largest estates in the region.
birmingham.site: Birmingham's Clean Air Zone covers everything inside the A4540 Middleway, so check delivery vehicles against it. In the Jewellery Quarter, send any planning conditions, because frame details are closely controlled.
birmingham.q: Can you work in the Jewellery Quarter?
birmingham.a: Send drawings, photographs and any planning conditions for the building. Frame profile and glazing can then be specified to what the conservation officer has approved.

west-sussex.meta: Commercial glazing in West Sussex for Crawley's Manor Royal, Chichester and coastal premises in Worthing. Send your schedule to our team.
west-sussex.lead: West Sussex runs from Gatwick and the Manor Royal business district down to Chichester's cathedral city and the south coast.
west-sussex.buildings: Manor Royal in Crawley is one of the South East's largest business districts, close to Gatwick Airport. Chichester holds the cathedral and the Goodwood estate nearby, while Worthing and Bognor Regis have seaside hotels, shops and care homes.
west-sussex.site: Near Gatwick, airside and security rules can affect access, so send any requirements. On the coast, tell us how exposed each elevation is, and in Chichester, share any conservation conditions.
west-sussex.q: Can you work in a care home on the West Sussex coast?
west-sussex.a: Yes. At Sunrise Care Home in Kettering we replaced every window and door in phases while residents stayed in. Send the layout and we can look at how your home could be phased.

west-yorkshire.meta: Commercial glazing across West Yorkshire: Bradford, Wakefield, Huddersfield and Halifax. Our Headrow Court project in Leeds shows the scale.
west-yorkshire.lead: Our Headrow Court project in Leeds is the closest published example of our work for anyone planning a scheme across West Yorkshire.
west-yorkshire.buildings: Bradford, Halifax and Huddersfield are rich in Victorian mills and civic buildings, and Saltaire is a World Heritage Site. The universities at Bradford and Huddersfield, plus Wakefield's business estates along the M1 and M62, add modern commercial premises.
west-yorkshire.site: Mill conversions tend to have many repeating openings in stone walls, so a schedule by elevation is the best starting point. Send any planning or listed building conditions with it.
west-yorkshire.q: Can you supply windows for a building conversion in West Yorkshire?
west-yorkshire.a: Yes. At Headrow Court in Leeds we supplied aluminium windows for four former office buildings converted into 108 student studios. Send your opening schedule and we can look at your scheme.

wiltshire.meta: Commercial glazing in Wiltshire for Swindon's business parks, Salisbury's cathedral city and heritage premises. Send your drawings to our team.
wiltshire.lead: Wiltshire stretches from Swindon's modern business parks to Salisbury's cathedral close and the World Heritage landscape of Stonehenge and Avebury.
wiltshire.buildings: Swindon holds many of the county's largest employers, the Great Western Hospital and the historic Railway Village. Salisbury and Marlborough have protected town centres, and Porton Down and the county's military sites bring specialist, secure premises.
wiltshire.site: Secure and military sites need vetting and access arrangements agreed in advance, so send those requirements early. In Salisbury and Marlborough, share any conservation conditions with your drawings.
wiltshire.q: Can you work on heritage buildings in Salisbury?
wiltshire.a: Send drawings, photographs and any planning or listed building conditions. The frames can then be specified against what has been approved.

worcestershire.meta: Commercial glazing in Worcestershire for Worcester, Redditch, Malvern and Kidderminster. Windows, doors and screens to your schedule.
worcestershire.lead: Worcestershire sits between the West Midlands and the Malvern Hills, with a cathedral city at its centre and strong engineering businesses around it.
worcestershire.buildings: Worcester holds the cathedral, the university and Worcestershire Royal Hospital, while Malvern Hills Science Park brings technology companies to the west. Redditch, Bromsgrove and Kidderminster have industrial estates, offices and schools.
worcestershire.site: Worcester's riverside and historic streets can restrict delivery vehicles, so tell us how the site is reached. For hospitals and schools, share which rooms can be released and when.
worcestershire.q: Can you work in an occupied hospital in Worcestershire?
worcestershire.a: Tell us which areas stay in use and how the building runs. At Herts and Essex Community Hospital we fitted colour-matched aluminium windows and doors in a working hospital without interrupting it.
